management.prescriber_action: New or unexplained warfarin + systemic-NSAID combination: confirm the anticoagulation plan (INR-monitoring plan + GI-bleed risk assessment) before supplying the NSAID; prefer paracetamol / alternative analgesia. Established, documented, monitored regimen: continue and monitor — do NOT interrupt warfarin.
management.monitoring: Check INR after starting AND after stopping the NSAID.
management.patient_counselling: Report urgent bleeding signs: melaena, haematemesis, unusual bruising, prolonged bleeding.

management.prescriber_action: Avoid omeprazole/esomeprazole with clopidogrel (they blunt CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel). Do NOT interrupt clopidogrel. Cimetidine is NOT a safe H2 alternative (it is itself a CYP inhibitor).
management.monitoring: Assess for reduced antiplatelet protection if the omeprazole/esomeprazole combination continues.
management.patient_counselling: Do not switch acid suppressants without advice; report cardiac symptoms.

evidence.excerpt: <verify - avoid omeprazole and esomeprazole with clopidogrel; they reduce active metabolite>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Omeprazole/esomeprazole reduce clopidogrel activation via CYP2C19 inhibition.

_action_note: confirm_and_monitor was misleading here — routine monitoring does not correct reduced clopidogrel activation; the operational action is to withhold/substitute the PPI, never to interrupt clopidogrel.

mechanism: Ibuprofen competitively blocks aspirin's irreversible COX-1 acetylation on platelets, antagonising aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect. The interaction is a pharmacodynamic timing effect: it applies principally to immediate-release low-dose aspirin plus a single/occasional ibuprofen dose, and dose separation preserves aspirin's action only while ibuprofen exposure is not continuous.

management.prescriber_action: To preserve aspirin cardioprotection: take ibuprofen at least 8 hours before, or at least 30 minutes after, the immediate-release low-dose (81 mg) aspirin dose (established for the specified single-dose scenario). Do NOT unilaterally stop specialist-directed antiplatelet therapy — clarify with the prescriber.
management.patient_counselling: For immediate-release low-dose aspirin: take the aspirin at least <verify: minimum interval IR low-dose aspirin must precede ibuprofen> BEFORE ibuprofen, OR take ibuprofen at least <verify: minimum interval ibuprofen must precede the aspirin dose> BEFORE the aspirin dose. Either order keeps ibuprofen out of the platelet-acetylation window. Spacing is undone if ibuprofen is taken repeatedly through the day.

timing.scenario: single-dose immediate-release 81 mg aspirin + 400 mg ibuprofen (FDA science paper)

management.exceptions: The 8-hour / 30-minute recommendation is established ONLY for the specified single-dose immediate-release scenario; data on chronic/repeated ibuprofen dosing are unclear, and it does not apply to enteric-coated aspirin or other NSAIDs. A separate additive-GI-bleeding rule (aspirin__nsaid_additive_gi_bleeding) must co-surface and must not be suppressed.

evidence.normalized_proposition: Ibuprofen 400 mg can blunt the antiplatelet effect of immediate-release 81 mg aspirin unless taken >=8 h before or >=30 min after (single-dose scenario).

mechanism: Aspirin plus another NSAID gives additive GI mucosal injury and bleeding risk, independent of the antiplatelet-timing question.

management.prescriber_action: Avoid routine concurrent NSAID with aspirin; if needed, lowest dose/shortest course and review gastroprotection.
management.monitoring: Watch for GI bleeding.
management.patient_counselling: Report GI bleeding (black stools, abdominal pain, vomiting blood).
management.exceptions: This additive-GI-risk warning applies to any aspirin+NSAID combination and is separate from the aspirin/ibuprofen antiplatelet-timing rule.

object.description: Dual antiplatelet therapy: aspirin PLUS a P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel/ticagrelor/prasugrel), both concurrently. Combined with the perpetrator oral anticoagulant this rule requires ALL THREE agents present.

mechanism: Triple antithrombotic therapy - aspirin PLUS a P2Y12 inhibitor PLUS an oral anticoagulant - produces additive antihaemostatic effects and substantially increases major bleeding risk. The combination is frequently an intentional, time-limited regimen (e.g. post-PCI in atrial fibrillation).

management.prescriber_action: This alert is intended to fire ONLY when all three antithrombotics are present together (aspirin AND a P2Y12 inhibitor AND an oral anticoagulant); it must NOT fire on any 2-of-3 pair (e.g. aspirin+warfarin, or DAPT alone). Confirm the indication and planned duration of triple therapy (frequently intentional and time-limited after PCI/ACS, e.g. atrial fibrillation post-stent). Do NOT independently stop any prescribed antithrombotic. If the overlap is unplanned or unexplained, urgently escalate to the prescriber. Assess bleeding risk and gastroprotection.
management.monitoring: Bleeding surveillance; ensure a documented stop/step-down (de-escalation) plan exists.
management.patient_counselling: Report any bleeding promptly; do not add OTC NSAIDs or aspirin; adhere to the planned course.
management.duration: Triple therapy is usually deliberately time-limited; confirm the intended duration and de-escalation plan.
management.exceptions: Intentional, prescriber-directed triple therapy is confirm-and-monitor; only unplanned or unexplained overlap is urgently escalated.

evidence.excerpt: <verify - triple antithrombotic therapy increases bleeding; minimise duration>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor plus an oral anticoagulant (triple therapy) markedly increases major bleeding risk; duration should be minimised.
